Level 3 · Advanced · Week 12

Showcase and Graduation

Share what you built, explain your choices, and plan what comes next.

What you will learn

  • Give a 2-minute design talk about one decision in your project.
  • Visit everyone’s project in a gallery walk and give helpful feedback.
  • Show what you have learned in the exit assessment.
  • Look back at your journey and plan your next steps, safely.

The big idea: explain the why

Anyone can say what their program does. A real developer can explain why they built it that way. In two minutes, pick one decision and walk through four steps:

Example: “Problem: my first ghost moved randomly and the game was too easy. Choice: I made a Chaser class that is a Ghost, and its move uses breadth-first search with a queue. Why: inheritance meant I only wrote the new part, and BFS always finds the shortest path. Next time: the Chaser is too clever – it should only chase every other turn.”

Good decisions to talk about: why you chose inheritance or composition, why a dictionary or a grid, which algorithm and why, what a test caught, what a playtester taught you.

Gallery walk: star and wish

Feedback helps when it is kind, specific and useful. “Cool!” is kind but not useful. “The score text was big and easy to read” is all three.

What next? Keep coding, safely

You can keep learning on your own. Some ideas: give your project a version 2; learn another Python library with a parent’s help; try a new kind of program (a text adventure, a simulation, a puzzle solver); teach someone younger what you know.

SafetyNext steps online

If you want to share your work or join a coding community, choose it together with a parent. Look for clear rules, moderators and a code of conduct. Use a nickname – never your real name, school, age, face or location, in the project or the account. Never move to private chats with strangers, never send photos, and tell an adult straight away if anything feels wrong. Your projects are yours: share only what you want to share.

New words

design decision
A choice about how to build something, with a reason.
feedback
Comments that help someone improve: kind, specific, useful.
showcase
An event where makers show and explain their work.
code of conduct
The rules a community agrees to, so everyone stays safe and respected.
version 2
The next, improved release of a project.

Homework: Showcase and Graduation

15–20 minutes. Your last homework of Level 3 – congratulations!

CoreA letter to future-you

Write a short letter to yourself to open in one year. Include: what you built, the bug you are proudest of fixing, a piece of advice for when coding gets hard, and one thing you want to be able to build by then.

ChallengeKeep coding: pick from the menu

Choose one item and plan your first step (with a parent, offline-first):

  • Version 2: add a level editor, a second enemy type or a settings file to your project. Commit each step.

  • New algorithm: write a maze generator using recursion, or sort a high-score table by two keys.

  • New data: run a (consent-first, anonymous) family survey and chart it.

  • New AI idea: train the monster sorter on your own made-up cards with three labels.

  • Teach it: show a younger friend or relative how to draw a fractal tree.

My choice and first step:

CreativeYour developer badge

Design a badge for yourself as a Level 3 graduate: a symbol that stands for your project, your nickname, and three skills you are proud of (e.g. “recursion”, “git”, “tests”).

Self-checkSelf-check: tick each box when it is true
